L7-M1.why: The README and the code disagree: README:94 promises a rendered `_headers`, but the static export drops it on purpose (code comment, SERVER-PROFILES §4, test) and nothing warns. Lowered because the kit is not in the shipped bundle and ADR-0015 forbids public hosting. The documented Cloudflare recipe uploads dist/, which has `_headers`, and the checklist requires curl -I plus a framing test. The meta CSP keeps script-src. Framing loses only defens
L7-M1.fix: Minimal: fix README:94 and PROFILE-README to say static/www omits `_headers` (it is the nginx/container root), and that `_headers` hosts should deploy dist/ per mirror-hosting.md. If support is wanted, render `_headers` at the static/www root, not <base>/ (Cloudflare and Netlify read only the root), with base-prefixed patterns. nginx already returns 404 for it.

L7-M3.why: The archive branch of openVerified never passes --expect-sha256 to extractArchive. parseArgs accepts the flag for every command, the directory branch rejects it (so it looks enforced), and verify's output tells operators to use it. A substituted archive that is consistent with its own manifest is profiled or previewed with exit 0. Reach is limited: documented recipes run verify --expect-digest first, USAGE lists the flag under verify only, and AD
L7-M3.fix: In openVerified's archive branch, validate both flags as verifyTarget does and pass expectedContentDigest and expectedArchiveSha256 to extractArchive, keeping the explicit mismatch messages. Add CLI tests for profile and preview with a wrong --expect-sha256. Hardening: reject options a command does not use (validate and package also ignore --expect-*).

L7-L2.why: --attr-source replaces only in-tree .gitattributes. git still reads $GIT_DIR/info/attributes, so a repo-local filter.*.clean runs during `git status`, contradicting the 'config-proof' comment. Exploiting it needs a hand-delivered .git directory (clone and fetch never transfer config or info/), and any git command in that directory would run the filter too. The documented use is the operator's own checkout; in CI, PR code already runs in the build
L7-L2.fix: Add --ignore-submodules=all to git status, and refuse when `git config --get-regexp '^filter\..*\.(clean|smudge|process)$'` (same env and -C) returns anything. A filter attribute without a driver does nothing, so no info/attributes check is needed. Alternatively drop git status and record only the commit (dirty: null, with a schema note). Add tests for info/attributes and submodules.

L7-L5.why: For a directory target, openVerified returns the original directory. policyFor, exportStatic and preview then re-read files without comparing them to the verified hashes. Anyone who can write to that directory can swap content after verification, and the profile still reports the verified digest. This needs hostile write access to the operator's input directory during the run (e.g. shared or synced dirs). Archives are safe: bytes are held in memo
L7-L5.fix: In openVerified's directory branch, copy regular files (O_NOFOLLOW, no symlinks) into a private mkdtemp dir. Run verifyDirectory with the expectations on that copy, use only the copy for policyFor, export and preview, and clean it up as for archives. The auditor's fix is correct; copying first and verifying the copy avoids passing bytes out of verifyDirectory.

L7-M2.why: Real: --commit is mandatory and the plan says it is verified (abort on FAIL), but selfhost.sh:221 calls verify-release.sh with 3 args, so the commit is never compared; it then extracts and runs up -d with no pause, though its own plan (:200) says to do the signed-tag/attestation checks 'then'. Needs an attacker-controlled download source or a downgrade (threat model 6.1). Passing the manifest alone does not help: a forged manifest passes.
L7-M2.fix: Before extracting, require an authenticity gate: --expect-sha256 carried from the separate-machine check, or gh attestation verify <tarball> --repo R --signer-workflow R/.github/workflows/release.yml --source-ref refs/tags/<tag>. Also require and pass --manifest (catches downgrade or mix-up). Stop before up -d unless the operator confirms.

L7-M4.why: Mechanism is real: pages.yml restores packages/*/dist from the main-scope libs cache and skips build:libs. Packages export ./dist/index.js and Vite has no alias, so a poisoned entry would ship. But Pages is workflow_dispatch and main only, the owner must enable it (docs: intentionally off), and the attacker needs code execution in a main-ref CI job (supply chain). The release tarball is unaffected (rm -rf dist). Unlikely preconditions, so Low.
L7-M4.fix: In pages.yml replace setup-node-libs with actions/setup-node + npm ci --ignore-scripts + rm -rf packages/*/dist && npm run build:libs, with no libs-cache restore. Better: publish the attested release tarball. The npm download cache is integrity-checked against the lockfile and can stay. This does not cover a compromised build-time dependency.

L7-L1.why: Real: the embed rules in _headers, deploy/nginx and infra lack ACAO, so the snippet in the v2 header (integrity + crossorigin=anonymous) is CORS-blocked. SRI without crossorigin is also blocked, so only a tag without SRI loads. embed-sri.mjs (adds ACAO, v1 only) is not wired into postbuild or release-build.sh. Hosts that send ACAO:* by default (GitHub Pages; Cloudflare Pages per its docs) are fine. Embedding is later-preserved, and harm needs a c
L7-L1.fix: Add Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * to the v1 and v2 embed rules in _headers (after the CORP line, for the embedHeaders.test.ts regex), deploy/nginx/nginx.conf, infra/proxy Caddyfile and nginx.conf, and infra/web/Caddyfile.static. For S3-10: extend embed-sri.mjs to v2, run it in release-build.sh, add routes for the hashed names, and publish the SRI value.

L7-L4.why: Logic holds: ci.yml:39 lists PR files through pulls/N/files, which GitHub caps at 3000. Truncation fails open: if only docs are seen, code=false, every heavy job is skipped, and the typescript and contracts gates pass on skipped. Exploiting it needs a maintainer to merge a PR of 3000+ files. CI on push to main always runs the full suite and release verify reruns the tests, so there is no direct impact. The aa*.md-before-apps/ ordering was not obs
L7-L4.fix: Fail safe: read changed_files with gh api repos/$REPO/pulls/$PR --jq .changed_files and set code=true when it is >= 3000 or larger than the number of filenames returned. Alternatively, build the list with git diff --name-only base...head in a checkout. The only side effect is that very large PRs run full CI.

L7-I1.why: check-headers.sh fails: the infra/proxy Caddyfile and ghostpay-headers.conf still send camera=() while _headers sends camera=(self); 4309eb8 fixed only deploy/nginx. The drift is stricter, so the effect is a broken QR camera on infra-hosted instances, not weaker security. infra/proxy and infra/web lack v2 embed routes and a dotfile deny, but dist has no dotfiles. CI does not run the script (already noted in audit-05 CI-15), yet infra/README.md:9
L7-I1.fix: Set camera=(self) in the infra/proxy Caddyfile, ghostpay-headers.conf and infra/web/Caddyfile.static. Add /ghostpay-embed-v2.js routes (CORP cross-origin, max-age=3600) and a dotfile deny. Extend check-headers.sh to cover Caddyfile.static and run it in the secrets-and-egress CI job.

L8-01.why: Real and by design: the beacon-only dev ceremony makes withdraw/ragequit proofs forgeable. Not shipped: pool-circuits and pool-contracts are outside the web and relayer closures, and the pool/registry constructors revert except on 31337 (no mainnet WETH9), 11155111 and 84532, so only valueless testnet pools can exist. DeployPool also needs ACK_INSECURE_DEV_CEREMONY. Shipped risk Info; Critical if these verifiers ever guard value. Owner-accepted (
L8-01.fix: None needed for beta. Before any value-bearing chain: phase 1 from Perpetual Powers of Tau and a public multi-party phase 2, plus a circuit audit. Keep isAllowedChain. Make DeployPool refuse verifiers whose vkey hash matches the committed dev SHA256SUMS. Add the pool and circuit contracts to CI and release gating (SUPPLY-CHAIN-CI-04).

L8-02.why: Repro confirms hooks run in the host realm. A plugin with no network grant called global fetch with a realm secret and kept running after TIMEOUT. Not shipped: nothing imports @ghostpay/plugin-api, there is no loader, and the bundle has 0 hits. Shipped risk Info. If wired into the web app: High with third-party plugins (key exfiltration via connect-src https:), Low with reviewed static first-party plugins. The limit is documented; isolation is st
L8-02.fix: None for beta. Before third-party plugins: run hooks in a dedicated Worker or a sandboxed iframe without allow-same-origin. Use a message-passing shim, terminate the worker on timeout, and set the worker CSP connect-src to the granted hosts only. Until then, allow only reviewed first-party static plugins, and restore the self-audit doc.

L8-03.why: Code matches: only Memory* stores exist, and the session checks seen.has then later seen.add, with a per-process in-flight set. A restart or a second process therefore reopens BIP-78 probing and re-entrancy. The host must pass a store, and docs mark Memory* test-only. Not shipped: btc-payjoin has no importer in any app or package. Shipped risk Info. A non-interactive receiver hosted on the memory store would be a Medium privacy leak (UTXO probing
L8-03.fix: None for beta. Before hosting a receiver: use a persistent store with an atomic addIfAbsent(outpoints) in place of has() then add(). Move Memory* to a test-only export, and have ReceiverSession refuse non-interactive mode unless the store declares persistence.

L8-04.why: Mechanism confirmed: PIR is tree-shaken today, but importing createScanSource ships the PIR client and the bundle still passes scanBundle(). No current impact (the code would still need deliberate wiring), so Low, not Medium. REACHABILITY checks out: pir-two-server is the only preserved package in the web closure, the relayer closure is clean, and BTC/Solana/Tron views ship ungated. VITE_FLAG_BITCOIN is an unchecked acceptance item, not an existi
L8-04.fix: Add an apps/web ESLint no-restricted-imports rule for '@ghostpay/scan-source' with importNames createScanSource, createPir2Source, createLightSource, createQuorumSource, describeScanMode and SCAN_MODE_CLAIMS. Add a preserved-code marker denylist to scan-bundle.mjs ('PIR server request failed', 'answer has wrong size', 'groth16'). Optionally move pir2 to a subpath export.

L8-05.why: Confirmed: validatePjUrl accepts https to any host, including private and link-local IP literals, and http to loopback on any port. The impact is smaller than stated. Plain-http metadata (169.254.169.254) is rejected, and https to an internal IP needs a valid cert. The real vector is a blind POST of the sender's PSBT to loopback, which is BITCOIN-08. Not shipped: no importer, and the web BTC view has no payjoin. Shipped risk Info; Low for a serve
L8-05.fix: Allow http loopback only when the network is regtest (BITCOIN-08). Outside regtest, reject IP-literal hosts that are not global unicast. Do not resolve DNS in the library. Server-side hosts must inject an egress-filtering fetch through the existing V1HttpOptions.fetch hook.

L8-06.why: Confirmed by repro: deleting the key from process.env does not scrub /proc/<pid>/environ, so POOL_RELAYER_KEY stays readable by the same uid, root and orchestrators. The README's 'removed from process.env' overstates the scrub. The Hardhat DEPLOYER_PRIVATE_KEY is a standard Sepolia-only pattern, and rpcUrl is operator config, not attacker input. Not shipped: there is no deploy recipe for pool-relayer, and keys are testnet-only. Shipped Info; Low
L8-06.fix: Add POOL_RELAYER_KEY_FILE using the apps/relayer secrets loader (regular file, no symlink, 0600, owner check) and prefer it to the env var. Fix the README wording. For Hardhat, use an encrypted keystore or a hardware signer instead of a raw env key.

L8-07.why: Confirmed. Export uses scrypt N=2^15 and an 8-character minimum, weaker than the shipped keystore (2^17, 14 characters, import cap 2^18). Import trusts the blob's logN up to 20: about 6.5 s synchronous and 970 MiB RSS in Node, worse in a mobile tab. Exploiting it needs an attacker-supplied backup (self-DoS) or a leaked blob for offline guessing. Not shipped: pool-sdk is used only by pool-relayer. Shipped Info; Low if enabled.
L8-07.fix: Reuse the web keystore profile. Export with N=2^17, r=8, p=1, a passphrase of at least 14 characters and NFKC. On import accept only logN in [14,18], pass maxmem 2^29, use scryptAsync, and bind v, logN and salt in the AES-GCM AAD.

L8-08.why: Confirmed. Over-limit bodies are drained to the end instead of closing the connection: 64 MiB was accepted against a 1 KiB cap. Node defaults apply (60 s headersTimeout, 300 s requestTimeout, no maxConnections), and there is no nosniff header. Memory stays bounded and the default bind is loopback. Not shipped: payer-sponsor has no process entry point and no deploy recipe. Shipped Info; Low if exposed (connection and bandwidth exhaustion). Not doc
L8-08.fix: When the body exceeds maxBodyBytes, answer 413 with Connection: close and call req.destroy(). Set headersTimeout=10_000, requestTimeout=15_000, maxConnections and keepAliveTimeout as pool-relayer does. Add X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff.

L8-09.why: Confirmed but benign. The exported PKCS8 key belongs to a self-signed cert for rpc/relay/gateway.example.test (reserved .test TLD), valid to 2126. Only net-harness's own test client trusts it. net-harness is private and only a devDependency of net-transport, its dist is gitignored, and no PRIVATE KEY string appears in the web or relayer bundles. Owner-accepted as H3. Info.
L8-09.fix: None required. Optional: export TEST_TLS_* only from a test-only subpath instead of the root index, so production code cannot import it by accident.

L3-F1.why: Real. Default is one RPC (settings.ts:20). A null or different hash for the saved anchor counts as a reorg to block 0; Scan.tsx persists invalidateFrom(0): every ledger record for that seller+chain is tombstoned, can't be re-saved or restored by import, no UI notice, plus a rescan from 0. Triggers: hostile RPC, stale load-balanced backend, or a node 1-100 blocks short of the anchor. Ledger integrity, no funds: Medium. THREAT_MODEL has single-RPC
L3-F1.fix: logs.ts:202: a null anchor is unavailable (RPC_FAILURE, retry), not a reorg. On a single-provider hash mismatch, quarantine records >= cutoff reversibly and rescan; tombstone only records the replacement scan no longer finds (or a second RPC confirms orphaned). With two RPCs, keep the old checkpoint when confirmRollback shows the old anchor still canonical on both.

L3-F2.why: Part (b) is real: with the opt-in second RPC, compareProviders uses fixed 1000-block chunks without halving, maps any error (2 MiB cap, -32602/-32005, rate limits) to secondary_error and needs secondary head >= primary page end. Page withheld, cursor held: ~1,950 spam logs in any 1000 blocks stall it until the user drops the second RPC; head lag withholds intermittently (r6 static heads overstate 'every run'). Medium. Part (a) duplicates L4-01/CH
L3-F2.fix: (b) compareProviders: halve on RESPONSE_TOO_LARGE/-32602/-32005 like fetchAnnouncements (or wrap the secondary in the windowed client) and end each page at min(primary, secondary) head via toBlock (or retry secondary_behind once after a block). (a), per L4-01: at one block, fetch router-caller logs (topics[3]) or use a larger streamed cap, then skip the rest visibly.

L3-F3.why: Mechanism real: one 60 s timer per worker batch (scanClient.ts:145,156), 'progress' replies ignored (:190-191), whole page up to 10,000 logs posted as one batch. Measured 3.37 ms/check (ECDH 86%, inherent to view tags; spending-key re-parse 3.4%): 10k page = 34 s, so devices >=1.8x slower than this 2.1 GHz Xeon time out on that page every run. Needs ~6-10k announcements in one page (spam); the cheaper L4-01 spam already halts all users. Low (lane
L3-F3.fix: Re-arm the reply timer on each 'progress' message for the pending batch (the worker already posts one per 128 logs), or post pages in <=1,000-log batches; keep an idle timeout for hung workers. Parsing the spending key once saves only ~3% (measured), so it is optional.

L3-F4.why: Real but needs a non-default setting. openSeen restarts at 0 each run, so a page whose non-router logs exceed the budget is deferred with the cursor held on every run (scanClient.ts:261,389-397). Router payments inside that page still show; later ones never do. Default 20,000 exceeds the 10,000 per-page cap, so the default is safe; the ungated Settings input (1-100000) and hint 'never skipped' make it reachable. Low. Undocumented; spec 05 and tes
L3-F4.fix: Guarantee progress: never defer the first page of a run, i.e. defer only when openSeen > 0 && openSeen + open > budget. Per-run work becomes budget + one page (<= 10,000), still under the 100,000 cap. Shrinking the page via maxLogs alone can still throw on one dense block.

L3-F5.why: Real: the second RPC gets exact getLogs ranges from the checkpoint and exact anchor reads, while the disclosure says 'the same scan ranges'. But the default 1000-block windowing barely hides position from the primary either: logs.ts and persistable() read eth_getBlockByNumber at the exact anchor, cursor+999 and new anchor. Opt-in second RPC; metadata only (scan position/cadence); verification requests are already disclosed. Low. Undocumented; ide
L3-F5.fix: Wrap the secondary in createWindowedScanClient with the same policy (fixes its getLogs ranges) and correct both RPC disclosure rows: each still learns the exact scan position from eth_getBlockByNumber at cursor, anchor and window-end heights. Full fix: grid-align window ends and checkpoint anchors (ideas/05 rule 7).

L3-F6.why: Real in what ships: the indexer source is a Settings option (no flag; Base Sepolia allowed) and the BTC view is in the default nav. Precondition: user picks a hostile/compromised https indexer or Esplora. Result: own-tab memory blowup or hang (Esplora has no timeout, only Cancel); no funds/keys unless unsaved in-memory keys die with the tab (user error). Doc comment promises a 'streamed size cap'. Esplora part duplicates L4-05; indexer part is ne
L3-F6.fix: Shared readCapped(res,max) using res.body.getReader() that cancels past the cap (as net-transport fetchTransport.ts:59-70), plus early Content-Length reject; use it in fetchHttpTransport and EsploraClient.text (byte cap, not UTF-16 length). Esplora: redirect:'error', cache:'no-store', linked AbortController with ~30s timeout. Proposed fix is correct; no side effects.

L3-F7.why: Profile verifies only against its own embedded signer, so any framer can mint one naming its origin; it adds no gate beyond nginx frame-ancestors, contrary to security-headers-embed.conf:7-8. Small impact: needs VITE_EMBED_IFRAME=1 (no recipe sets it), the embed conf and an operator-allowlisted framer that embeds the invoice itself; it gets status/chainId/txHash, about what the payer knows. Embed is later-preserved. DEVIATIONS 6 notes only the mi
L3-F7.fix: When embed is promoted: pass the parsed invoice signer to notifyEmbedDone and post only if its signature is valid and invoice.signer === profile.signer (spec 14 already signs profiles with the ADR-0002 invoice key). Operator-key pinning adds key management and duplicates frame-ancestors. Now: fix security-headers-embed.conf:7-8 and DEVIATIONS 6 to say frame-ancestors is the only gate.

L3-F8.why: Dead code confirmed: csp.mjs/embed-sri.mjs were wired at 9654e9a (vite plugin + postbuild) and lost in consolidation tree 8672a9a. README now correctly says postbuild runs only scan-bundle, so no operator doc asks for GHOSTPAY_CONNECT_ORIGINS. Underlying S3-10/S3-11 are documented open (audit 03; 05/web-app.md:124-125). v2 header still advises SRI, which also fails without ACAO (L7-L1, overlap). Info.
L3-F8.fix: Restore the 9654e9a wiring (transformIndexHtml + closeBundle on dist/_headers; postbuild embed-sri then scan-bundle) AND let scan-bundle accept the configured origins (else build fails), extend embed-sri to v2, add ACAO/CORP/immutable rules for hashed files in deploy/nginx and infra (L7-L1). Or delete both scripts and drop the SRI advice from the v2 header.

L3-F9.why: Real: slot key and vault scope are sha256(spendPub|viewPub), computable from the public meta-address, and 'Wipe keys from memory' (clearSession) touches no storage. Needs browser-profile access; reveals the device-seller link and scan progress only, no keys/funds. Documented: PRIVACY-E2E-09 (Info, open; written for v1 key, now more linkable) and ADR-0025 accepts the visible vault scope id. Duplicate of lane-1 I-1.
L3-F9.fix: Minimal: list these identifiers in the THREAT_MODEL browser-profile row and privacy docs, and add an explicit, confirmed 'forget this seller's local scan data' action. Do not auto-clear on memory wipe: it deletes encrypted reconciliation history and forces rescans. HMAC/HKDF(viewing key) ids need migration: scope id is in vault AAD, HKDF info and record ids.

L5-01.why: Real: the in-lane check only refuses permit.deadline<=now. The permit is outside the sweep signature and the quote MAC, and the contract swallows a failed permit, so a permit that lapses before inclusion gives a mined revert the relayer pays for. The strike is recorded only afterwards. Not High for the beta: the loss is relayer gas, capped by the loss and daily budgets. The 429-for-everyone result needs about 10 gwei per revert. That is far above
L5-01.fix: Refuse when permit.deadline < sweep.deadline, reusing permit_expired (already a PRE_BROADCAST class), at service.ts:573 or in validation. Add no margin: web sweep.ts:169,247 and hops execute.ts:61-84 sign permit.deadline == sweep.deadline, so '+margin' would reject every honest request. The sweep deadline (>now+30 s) then bounds the window.

L5-02.why: Real: all users share the global loss cap. Once it is spent, every sweep gets 429 for the window, mined reverts stay breaker-neutral and healthz stays ok. It is worse than stated: the global cap is reserved and settled once per key (dst+net), so it trips at half the configured loss. Medium, not High: the cap fails closed by design and is alerted. With beta-chain gas and the example budget it needs far more reverts per hour than a one-tx-per-recei
L5-02.fix: Charge the global cap once per sweep: reserve it separately from the per-key reservations. Keep a slice of the global cap for sources with no loss in the window, so one source group cannot 429 everyone. Alert or degrade health on a sustained mined_revert rate. Fixing L5-01 removes the cheap source of reverts.

L5-06.why: Real: on a receipt timeout the daily-budget reservation is kept until UTC midnight, and both loss-budget reservations until the window ends. The lane is held for receiptTimeoutSeconds, and nothing bumps the fee or cancels. The breaker already recorded success at broadcast, so healthz stays ok. Medium: breaker and health silently miss stuck txs, and a stall needs a fee spike or sequencer stall. Budget exhaustion is negligible at beta gas; the main
L5-06.fix: After a receipt timeout, record a breaker failure explicitly and alert. The job's permit is already settled at broadcast, so a setOutcome there is too late. Keep the reservation in a pending ledger that a later receipt lookup releases. Replace-by-fee or cancel the head nonce.

L5-08.why: The default is 0 as stated, but it has no impact on the beta chain. The reserve scales only the gas term, and at L2 gas prices the 50 bps floor sets the fee, so even the 5000 bps maximum changes nothing for typical amounts. It is a pricing knob, not a control: attacker reverts pay no fee anyway. It is documented as a default still to be tuned.
L5-08.fix: None for the beta. Before enabling a high-gas chain, require an explicit per-chain griefReserveBps in config and refuse startup on non-testnet chains without it. Avoid a global non-zero default, which would raise every fee.

L5-10.why: Real: gasPrice() turns RPC errors into RelayerError rpc_unavailable, and the first in-lane call runs outside op(). Both op() and the default outcome treat that as neutral, so a full RPC outage never opens the breaker and healthz stays 200. Low, a monitoring gap: during an outage quotes fail too, so the service is down either way, and error-level logs and 503 metrics still show it. It is not attacker-triggerable. The runbook wrongly says the break
L5-10.fix: The proposed op() wrap does not work: gasPrice() already throws a RelayerError, which op() rethrows without setting the outcome. Use op(() => this.d.gasPrices.getGasPrice(chainId)), then apply the cap check, at both service.ts:548 and :603. gas_price_too_high must stay neutral.

L5-03.why: Real: server.ts:296-300 spends the single global quote token before the CT/body checks (301-303). Ordering is not the root cause: valid JSON quotes are as cheap (gas price cached 3 s), so 'charge after validation' alone changes nothing. ~21+ IPv4 /32s or one /48 (no per-/48 rate) deny every quote, so every relayed sweep. Relayer is optional, direct sweep remains, no funds at risk: Medium. Known RELAYER-01 (P1 open); audit 17 wrongly calls it boun
L5-03.fix: Reordering alone is cosmetic. Add a per-/24 and per-/48 group limiter ahead of the global take, single-flight the quote gas-price cache and raise or drop the global cap (quotes are CPU-cheap), then take the global token after parseQuoteRequest; alert on rate_limited_global. Durable fix per RELAYER-01: let /v1/sweep price the fee itself so sweeps do not need a quote.

L5-04.why: Real: groupSpends (limiter.ts:378-393) never evicts and salted keys rotate daily, so after maxKeys groups ever seen all newcomers share overflowGroupSpend; one sweep's dst and net reservations both hit it. 'One revert 429s all' is overstated: on Base Sepolia at default perKeyWei the lockout needs ~2.5k-25k reverts/hour (serial lane can't) and zero-loss refusal needs gasLimit*price >2.5e15 (above the 5 gwei cap): Low. Medium on ~0.1-5 gwei chains
L5-04.fix: Evict stale groups like the key table: hold groups in a BoundedTable whose idle test is window != current window, so a full table only overflows on live entries. Give dst and net keys separate overflow buckets so one sweep is not reserved twice against one shared group. Emit a metric when a reservation uses an overflow entry.

L5-05.why: Real: in deploy/ compose the relayer's peer is the nginx container, not in the example trustedProxies, so XFF is ignored and all clients share one bucket of 30/min, burst 10 (quote+sweep; junk counts, since ipLimiter runs before the CT check). One IP at 0.5 req/s denies the relayer to everyone. The proposed fix is incomplete: nginx sets XFF=$remote_addr, the docker gateway of the host TLS terminator for every client. Recipe untested, no project r
L5-05.fix: nginx: set_real_ip_from <host gateway IP only>; real_ip_header X-Forwarded-For; real_ip_recursive on (TLS terminator overwrites XFF), keep XFF $remote_addr. Pin the backend subnet in compose and set relayer trustedProxies to it. Replace trustProxyHops in deploy/config/README.md. selfhost.sh: warn when trustedProxies is loopback-only. Re-test with two client IPs.

L5-07.why: Real doc drift: deploy/config/README.md:5 says trustProxyHops 1; the strict parser rejects unknown keys -> 'fatal: config $: invalid' (key not named), api crash-loops, /api 502. Fails closed. Removing the key leaves loopback-only trustedProxies, which is L5-05. Duplicate of L7-L3's README half and the root of L5-05's misconfig. The same stale key is also in docs/operators/relayer-runbook.md and docs/developer/api/apps.md. Ops/docs only: Low.
L5-07.fix: Replace trustProxyHops in deploy/config/README.md, docs/operators/relayer-runbook.md and docs/developer/api/apps.md with trustedProxies guidance that matches the L5-05 fix. Make the config parser name the unknown key and hint that trustProxyHops was replaced by trustedProxies.

L7-L3.why: Two halves. The README/trustProxyHops to one-bucket half duplicates L5-07 and L5-05 (Medium there). Unique part: deploy/nginx 'location /api/' proxies any path, so /api/metrics reaches the relayer, unlike infra/proxy (4-route allowlist, /metrics 404). Compose sets no metricsTokenEnv, so /metrics is 404 by default; when enabled it needs a 32-256 char bearer compared in constant time. Defense in depth: Low. 'Trust the web subnet' alone does not res
L7-L3.fix: Allowlist routes: location ~ ^/api/(healthz|v1/info|v1/quote|v1/sweep)$ { rewrite ^/api(/.*)$ $1 break; proxy_pass http://api:8787; ... } and return 404 for every other /api/ path, including /api/metrics; scrape metrics from inside the backend network. For buckets apply the L5-05 fix (nginx real_ip plus pinned backend trustedProxies).

F1.why: Real but narrower. The waiver needs an existing allowance (Factory.sol:162). A paused FiatToken rejects approve/permit, so a caller without one cannot deploy until unpause. A blacklisted factory blocks approve only on FiatToken <=v2.1; in v2.2 approve/permit check only pause, so the permanent case fails for current USDC. Any standing approver can deploy every account without paying. Not shipped: flag off, no deployment, the runbook says do not de
F1.fix: Operational: FLAT_FEE=0 for pausable fee tokens (the README already advises this), or keep a funded, pre-approved deployer of last resort (waived deploys do not use up its allowance). In-contract alternative: charge the fee in native coin. Correct DEVIATIONS P7 and contracts-reference.md:150. Add a FiatToken-like mock (approve/permit whenNotPaused) test.

F2.why: Confirmed. payERC20WithBuffer sends msg.value to A_acct, a contract that cannot spend it as gas (withdrawals are relayable signatures). With a non-zero limitsRoot and no address(0) leaf, native requestWithdraw always reverts InvalidLimitProof; no rescue (L-05, by design). Only the policy-scheme builder option produces it: web pay.ts never passes a buffer, the flag is off, nothing is deployed. Loss bounded to a small payer-chosen buffer. Low. L-05
F2.fix: Remove the buffer option from buildPolicyPaymentTx now. Before any policy-router deployment, either delete payERC20WithBuffer (A_acct never needs gas) or forward msg.value to policy.owner, the EOA that can spend it. Owner and policyHash are already in calldata, so this links nothing new.

F3.why: Confirmed. Code and generated ABI use PolicyRef{owner, policyHash}. Developer docs describe the N-01 salt ABI and its selectors as shipped and say undeployed accounts stay unlinkable. Cause: consolidation commit 8672a9a re-imported the pre-N-01 router, dropping 50881e4's salt change and the DEVIATIONS R10-R13 the docs still cite. The linkability is tracked as PRIVACY-E2E-05 (open); DEVIATIONS R2/R3 and CONTRACTS_SPEC s4 match the code. Scheme 2 i
F3.fix: Now: correct the three developer docs to the PolicyRef ABI and selectors, remove references to the missing DEVIATIONS R10/R11, and mark N-01/PRIVACY-E2E-05 open. Before any scheme-2 deployment, re-port 50881e4's salt-only router with its builders, decoder, ABI and tests. Even then, policyHash becomes public once an account is deployed.

F4.why: Confirmed as a defense-in-depth gap. EXPECTED_POLICY_FACTORY_CODEHASH is optional, pre-deploy-check has no policy-router mode, the manifest schema has no policyRouter, and the flagged web view only reads back user-typed factory/router addresses. Testnet-only (chain.testnet check), flag off, nothing pinned, warning banner shown. Already tracked in DEVIATIONS R6/R9, CONTRACTS-CORE-04, CHAIN-ADAPTERS-08 and N3. The finding's DeployPolicyRouter line
F4.fix: Before enabling scheme 2 on any network: add policyRouter and its runtime codehash to the schema and the signed manifest, and have the web app read pins only from there. Make the factory and implementation codehash pins mandatory outside local chains. Add a policy-router mode to pre-deploy-check.sh. The factory codehash also pins its immutables.

F5.why: Confirmed. verifyReceipt returns 'verified' for any final viaRouter claim with no token allowlist, balance check or transfer evidence; the router accepts any token, so a junk-token router payment reads as verified. No callers: the web scan marks verified only when verifyClaimedPayment says received and final; apps/web's own verifyReceipt is a separate signed-receipt helper. Private package. Known as the router half of CHAIN-ADAPTERS-04; the 09 de
F5.fix: Delete verifyReceipt and its tests, keeping the ReceiptStatus type (apps/web/src/lib/scanClient.ts uses it). Alternatively, make it delegate to verifyClaimedPayment. Nothing else calls it.

F6.why: Confirmed, but by design. A CREATE2 address depends on the exact init code; the local 0.8.28 build with cbor_metadata=false can never produce 0x5564..5564, so the script needs ALLOW_NONCANONICAL_ANNOUNCER and Deploy needs ALLOW_CUSTOM_ANNOUNCER. Matters only on chains without the canonical announcer, which the testnet runbook checks first. Impact is interop with third-party ERC-5564 scanners; GhostPay scans the manifest's announcer. Documented in
F6.fix: None required. Optionally, note in the runbook that a custom announcer hides payments from third-party ERC-5564 wallets. Reproducing the canonical address would need the exact upstream init code and salt.

L1-01.why: Reproduced in the default UI: Generate keys -> Create invoice (no backup gate or prompt) -> 15 min without pointerdown/keydown (scroll, mousemove, focus, visibilitychange do not re-arm; a background tab idles) -> clearSession() destroys the only copy. Payments to the still-valid invoice (24 h default, up to 90 d) or the shared meta-address are unspendable forever. Needs a skipped backup (not Critical), but app copy says keys stay until wipe/close
L1-01.fix: Track a per-session durable-copy flag (keystore, vault or hex import; keystore download; vault save). Until set, the idle lock locks tags only and shows a visible banner. Gate Create invoice and meta-address copy/QR/registry behind 'Back up now' or a typed waiver (spec idea 04). Fix settings.lock.hint, DEVIATIONS 11, troubleshooting.md:25 and the web README.

L1-02.why: Confirmed in the UI. With a vault saved, Sweep refuses without the passphrase. But 'Delete encrypted vault' then 'Confirm' needs none; after that Sweep shows no field and broadcasts. 'Download encrypted keystore' exports all keys under any new passphrase. So the gate labelled 'required for each sweep' does not stop the walk-up or unattended-tab attacker it targets. It needs access to an unlocked tab with keys loaded inside the 15 min window: a sa
L1-02.fix: Tie the gate to the session: keep the vault ciphertext in memory when keys are unlocked from or saved to the vault, and check every sweep against it even if IndexedDB is emptied. Require the same step-up for keystore export and for deleting a vault whose meta.metaAddress equals the loaded identity. Let a non-matching vault be deleted, showing its meta.metaAddress; it blocks all sweeps.

L1-04.why: Confirmed in the App UI. 'Wipe keys from memory' only calls clearSession(), so the tag vault keeps A's derived keys. Identity B loaded in the same tab finds tags already unlocked. B's tag saves (or archive imports) are encrypted under A's profile: A can read them later, and B can never open them again. Only the idle path locks tags. Export and rotate re-check the viewing key. It needs two identities in one tab or profile and leaks only labels and
L1-04.fix: Lock the tag vault on every session change (subscribe in App.tsx, or call services.vault.lock() wherever clearSession/install runs). Take captureSessionGuard() in Scan/TagArchive unlock and save, so an unlock or save started under identity A cannot finish after the keys change.

L1-06.why: Confirmed. passphraseProblem gates the vault, keystore, tag archive and invoice passphrases. It uses only character classes, length and a 13-word denylist. Repeats of the app name, season or year with symbols, and keyboard walks pass; the estimator scores some as 'strong' (that label is not shown in the UI). Exploiting it needs the ciphertext (profile copy or keystore file) and a user who picks such a phrase. scrypt N=2^17 slows rule-based guessi
L1-06.fix: Offer, and pre-fill by default, a generated 5-6 word EFF-wordlist passphrase. Before the score threshold, have passphraseStrength penalise repeated halves or substrings, keyboard walks, years/months/seasons padded with symbols, 'ghostpay', and a small bundled common-password list. Keep scrypt N=2^17.

L1-07.why: Confirmed. requireSession opens the spending, viewing and signing scalars and keeps them in `issued` until clearSession (at most 24). Scan needs only the viewing key and invoice creation only the signing key, so a plaintext spending key stays on the heap for the session, defeating the SecretBox design. It matters only to heap-reading attackers (debugger, extension, memory dump): defense in depth, Low. Same as audit 05 WEB-APP-07, which was never
L1-07.fix: At Scan.tsx:152 and :444 use revealViewingKey() (runScan and TagVault.unlock already wipe it). In invoiceCreate.ts use withSessionSecrets((s) => signInvoice(invoice, s.signingKey)). Move test/keys.ts to withSessionSecrets, then delete requireSession and `issued`.

I-1.why: Confirmed. Wiping keys leaves localStorage checkpoint keys and IndexedDB reconciliation records named by an unsalted SHA-256 of the public spend and view keys (derivable from the meta-address), plus chain ids and scan heights. Someone with profile access and a candidate meta-address can confirm the device used that identity. No funds or secrets are exposed. The THREAT_MODEL browser-profile row does not mention it. Info.
I-1.fix: Document in THREAT_MODEL.md:30 and the user docs that scan checkpoints and encrypted reconciliation records stay until site data is cleared, keyed by a public-key hash. Optionally add 'forget this identity's local data'. Salting keyId (HMAC with a per-profile random salt) also works but needs a storage migration.

I-3.why: Confirmed. validatePayload checks only `.length` of invoiceLabel and notes, so null, numbers, booleans, objects and arrays pass and survive save/list. The tag archive import path (strict JSON) feeds this function. Nothing renders these fields and the UI never sets them, so there is no current impact. Info.
I-3.fix: In validatePayload, reject invoiceLabel and notes unless typeof === 'string', and apply the clientLabel trim and length rules, so stored and imported tags keep the declared TagPayload type.

L1-03.why: Real. Default is one RPC: a null or changed hash for the saved checkpoint block rolls back to 0, and Scan.tsx persists invalidateFrom(0): every record is tombstoned and can't be re-saved, even after Delete (same root as L3-F1). New here: after any invalidation, records verified later restore as invalidated on a fresh profile, and the preview under-counts. Correction: a real tip reorg on a consistent RPC throws 'retry'. Ledger only, but beta-core
L1-03.fix: logs.ts:202,310: a null checkpoint/window block is RPC_FAILURE (retry), not a reorg. invalidateFrom: tombstone only records whose stored blockHash is no longer canonical at their height (second RPC if set), not all >= cutoff. Import: skip the cutoff for records saved after the invalidation (store its time), let a live save clear a non-tombstoned downgrade, preview via the activation merge.

I-2.why: Real, no direct impact. Export walks services.chains (compile-time CHAINS.filter(enabled)), so stored history, invoice registrations and receipts for a chain this build doesn't list are left out and not counted in the warning. All 7 testnets are enabled now and no mainnet ever was, so it needs a later build that narrows chains. The data stays in IndexedDB, and import fails closed on unknown chains. The panel ships (SellerKeys.tsx:353) but is late
I-2.fix: On export, list this seller's stored vault keys (IDB getAllKeys on 'vaults', prefix sellerKeyId:) and name chains the build doesn't list in the 'NOT in this archive' warning. Optionally carry them as opaque ciphertext and let import skip unknown chains with a warning instead of refusing the whole archive.

L4-01.why: Real on default stack: permissionless canonical announcer, 2 MiB client cap; logs.ts rethrows RESPONSE_TOO_LARGE at a 1-block window and its read/log caps throw, not truncate; runScan rethrows. Every seller whose cursor precedes the block fails there each run (any RPC), also hiding earlier payments in that fetch. ~12M gas once, free on Base Sepolia, repeatable; only a blind manual restart past it recovers: cheap service-wide detection outage. Aud
L4-01.fix: logs.ts:268-282: if the log budget or read cap would be exceeded after a completed window, stop there with truncated=true. Progress is guaranteed: a window needs at most 999 reads, and a 2 MiB block holds under 2,100 logs. For a 1-block RESPONSE_TOO_LARGE, re-query with topics[3]=router (widen assertScanFilter) and report the skipped open lane. Also halve on other result-limit errors.

L4-02.why: Real: deep scan lists a wrong-tag router payment as verified with a Sweep button, but both sweep paths call deriveStealthSecret, which throws VIEW_TAG_MISMATCH even though the address check proves control. It needs a non-GhostPay or tampered payer (the app's pay path always uses the derived tag), who gains nothing. The error is loud and the key is still derivable from the seller's keys, so funds can be recovered with exported keys or a fixed buil
L4-02.fix: Add an opt-in option to deriveStealthSecret (e.g. { allowTagMismatch: true }) that skips only the tag compare at stealth.ts:211 and keeps the ZERO_STEALTH_KEY and ADDRESS_MISMATCH checks. Pass it from deriveVerifiedSweepKey, which already checks addressOfSecret === owner. Defaults and vectors stay the same. Update THREAT_MODEL D4 and receive-and-scan.md, which still say deep scan is not built.

L1-05.why: Real: onCheckStatus writes the result for the lock captured at render with no compare-and-swap. Navigation unmounts Sweep, so 'checking' resets; a slow but successful check #1 (createClient: 10 s x 3 tries per call) can land after check #2 and a newly signed order and replace that order's lock, re-arming signing. Impact small: pending orders share balance and permit nonce, so at most one runs, to the user's own destination. Needs a signed 84532 m
L1-05.fix: Add a CAS helper in state.tsx (resolveSweepAttempt(expected, next)) that writes only if the stored lock for (chain, owner) still has the same identity (order relayer+nonce, or expectedHash+nonce) and is unresolved, merging the new status into the stored lock; use it in onCheckStatus. The auditor's fix is right; compare identity fields, not object reference.

L2-F1.why: Real: createClient keeps only the JSON-RPC code ('RPC_FAILURE: json-rpc error 3'), so REVERT_TEXT never matches and every revert is 'unavailable', which callers ignore. Loss is gas only and mostly covered elsewhere: eth_estimateGas stops ERC-20 direct sweeps first, wallets estimate payments, and native sweeps on Base Sepolia fail earlier (L2-F2). Defense in depth, so Low (auditor: Medium). Extends WALLET-SAFETY-05 (Low, open), which assumed regex
L2-F1.fix: In rpc.ts parseResponse set a sanitized flag on ChainAdapterError (reverted = code 3, or -32000/-32015 with /revert/ in the message; no message text kept). simulateCall refuses on it (keep REVERT_TEXT for EIP-1193 errors). Show 'unavailable' as a warning, not a hard block. Pass gas in the direct-sweep dry run. Test through createClient with a node-like transport.

L2-F2.why: Native sweep sets value = balance - 21000*maxFee, so tx cost equals the balance exactly. OP-stack txpool and consensus also charge the L1 data fee (op-geth TotalTxCost, buyGas), so any L1 fee > 0 rejects it. Base Sepolia, the beta chain, is OP-stack; native ETH is the default invoice asset and has no relayer path, so native payments cannot be swept, and each try jams the tab's lock (receipt-only resolution). Funds stuck, not lost. (b) and (c) are
L2-F2.fix: Reserve the L1 fee: on OP-stack chains call GasPriceOracle (0x42..0F) getL1Fee(unsigned tx) with a margin and subtract it; elsewhere set gas from eth_estimateGas({from, to: dest, value}) (covers Arbitrum and contract/7702 destinations) and pass gas to the dry run. To unjam, allow a same-nonce re-sign (no double-spend); a finalized-nonce check alone never fires because nothing consumes the nonce.

L2-F3.why: Real: verifySubmission stops after 6 reads (7.5 s), pollReceipt checks only receipt.to, and the tx is never re-fetched, so the UI says 'included in block N' and the local receipt/proof says 'included' with previewed amounts. A malicious wallet controls broadcast timing, so it can skip the check at will; no slow RPC is needed. Still Low: it needs a malicious wallet that could steal anyway, the UI says 'could not be checked', and the proof is label
L2-F3.fix: In submitTx, when a receipt exists and verification was 'not-visible-yet', fetch the tx again and run the same comparison (throw SubmissionMismatchError on mismatch); if it is still unavailable, mark it unverified. Pay.tsx, buildReceipt and PaymentProofQr must not show or record 'included' unless verified ('no-rpc' keeps its label). The auditor's fix is right.

L2-F4.why: Real: in fixed_token mode the signed fiat total comes only from line items (invoiceCreate.ts:119,138) and reviewInvoice only checks items+tax vs fiat (pay.ts:81-84), so Pay shows 'Invoice total USD 10.00' beside 'Fixed: 1000 USDC' with no warning. Payee-crafted misdirection; the true token amount is shown 3+ times (Pricing, You pay, Final check) and in the wallet, so Low. Reachable in the 84532 beta (fixed_token is the only mode there). Audit 03
L2-F4.fix: In fixed_token mode relabel the row 'Seller-stated fiat total (not checked; you pay the token amount)' and make the token amount the headline total; add a non-blocking warning when USDC/EURC differs from a USD/EUR fiat total by >1%; mirror a hint in CreateInvoice. Never block (surcharges are legitimate), no feeds needed.

L2-I1.why: Real but latent: readPrice maxAge = clamp(quote TTL,60,86400) taken from the seller-signed invoice (pay.ts:150); maxSlippageBps is only displayed (Pay.tsx:895); price is not re-read in buildFinal. Only FEEDS entry is Sepolia ETH/USD, no heartbeat (quote.ts:46-59). Default build bundles no manifest and beta chain 84532 has no feed, so fiat_quote is unpayable in what ships; fiat/oracles are later-preserved (LEAN_RELEASE_SCOPE.md). Info.
L2-I1.fix: Before enabling a feed on any shipped chain: cap price age app-side (min(TTL, heartbeat+margin, e.g. 3600 s)), re-read the price at buildFinal/just before send and refuse if the amount moved more than maxSlippageBps from the reviewed amount, or drop the slippage text. Fix the API doc drift.

L2-I2.why: Real: schema accepts expiresAt and quote timestamps up to 2^53-1 (schema.ts:293-299); formatUnix throws RangeError above 8.64e12 s; Pay renders it (Pay.tsx:900; :895 for fiat_quote) and apps/web has no error boundary, so React 19 unmounts the whole root. Reachable in the default build (details render without a manifest). Impact small: attacker link only blanks that tab, fragment is already cleared so reload recovers; no funds or keys. Info.
L2-I2.fix: Make formatUnix total (fallback text when the Date is invalid), add a reviewInvoice blocker for timestamps past a sane horizon (e.g. > 253402300799 or now+10y), and wrap ViewSwitch in an error boundary that shows an error panel instead of unmounting.

L2-I3.why: Real: call() maps 4001 to UserFacingError, which sendViaWallet rethrows after beginAttempt, leaving 'unknown' (wallet.ts:312-330); retry needs explicit clear. That part is deliberate and test-asserted (Pay.test.tsx:472-488). Undocumented: approve/revoke keys are calldata+account (wallet.ts:270-274; payExec.ts:164,183), so an identical approval or revoke for a later invoice is blocked even after success. Approvals are only used for buffer/permit f
L2-I3.fix: Scope approval/revoke keys by invoice digest, or exempt them (approve sets, not adds, so a duplicate only costs gas). Optionally (owner decision; current test asserts otherwise) treat EIP-1193 4001 on eth_sendTransaction as not sent and drop the pre-send record; keep 'unknown' for all other errors.

L2-I4.why: Real: Pay/Sweep/Scan read back through verifyManifestForFlow/verifyManifestState -> verifyManifestOnChain with one client (manifest.ts:107-126; deploymentsVerify.ts:44-70), even with a secondary RPC set; two-provider verifyDeployment is reached only from lib/deployment.ts, imported only by hardening.test.ts. Manifests are bundled and release-signed, so a lying RPC can only pass an already-wrong signed manifest. Info; applies only to signed-manife
L2-I4.fix: Pass app.getSecondaryRpc() into verifyManifestForFlow and the Scan check and call verifyDeployment(m, primary, { secondary }) (also enforces the canonical announcer), failing closed on disagreement as Scan does; delete or wire lib/deployment.ts; correct apps/web/deployments/README.md.

L4-I1.why: Real: the production scheme (build validator, web loadBundledManifest, relayer config.ts:225, ops-monitor) signs keccak256(canonicalManifestJson) with no domain tag; the legacy domain-tagged text scheme is still exported and the bare name verifyManifestSignature is the legacy one. No impact today: canonical JSON starts with '{' so it cannot collide with RLP tx, EIP-191 or EIP-712 preimages, and the release key is dedicated. Audit 05 credited a do
L4-I1.fix: Before the first real release signature, sign keccak256(utf8('GhostPay.DeploymentManifest.v2\0') || canonicalJson), or EIP-191 over a domain-tagged text so standard signers work without raw-hash signing; re-sign the e2e fixture; remove or rename the legacy verifyManifestSignature/verifyTextManifestSignature exports.

L4-I3.why: Real: SecretBytes (secret.ts:29-59) blocks toString/toJSON/slice/subarray but not toHex/toBase64 (in current browsers) or ES2023 toReversed/with; secret.ts:15-18 already calls it a guardrail, not a boundary (S3-08); no shipped call site. buildLookupCall uses isAddress strict:false (registry.ts:114) on raw RegistryView input; the lookup is read-only and shows the normalized registrant, so a typo only yields a wrong or empty lookup. Info.
L4-I3.fix: (a) Add throwing overrides for toHex, toBase64, toReversed, toSorted and with in SecretBytes and keep the 'not a boundary' wording; (b) in buildLookupCall use isAddress(registrant, { strict: true }) (all-lowercase still accepted) and report a checksum mismatch instead of normalizing.

L4-03.why: Real: both electrs forks return 4xx when start >= tx count (Blockstream 400, mempool 404), so any block with a multiple of 25 txs throws TRANSPORT_FAILURE and the whole scan (always to the tip) is lost; a payment followed by such a block is undetectable in the UI. Ships in default nav, but the BTC view is test-network-only (mainnet off), later-preserved, fails loudly, coins stay recoverable: Low, not Medium. Fixture, shim and live e2e use []-sema
L4-03.fix: Get the count first (GET /block/:hash tx_count or /block/:hash/txids, both in both forks), fetch exactly ceil(n/25) pages, require page len = min(25, n-start) and txids equal to the list. Drop the /block/:hash/raw option: raw blocks lack the prevout scripts BIP-352 tweaks need. Make the fixture and regtest shim return 4xx past the end; add 25/50-tx tests.

L4-04.why: Real: linked starts with only genesis and a new source per scan, so only a scan from height 1 reaches genesis; UI windows are <=500 blocks to tip, so on testnet4/signet the first block's parent is never checked. Forgery itself is the known BITCOIN-03 low-work-fork limit (SCAN_LIMITS[0], user doc); anchoring would not stop a forged tip. Impact is an overclaim in a test-only view: Low (borderline Info). 'Never' is overstated: true for regtest from
L4-04.fix: Correct the text: 'Consecutive blocks within one scan must link by previous-block hash; the first scanned block is not linked to earlier blocks', and scope :14 to prevout edits ('cannot invent one by altering these; a low-work fork can'). Fix the same claim in docs. HeaderChain anchoring needs absent checkpoints and still admits a forged min-difficulty tip on testnet4.

L4-05.why: Real: the Solana client has no cap; Esplora (16 MiB) and Tron (8 MiB) check only after res.text() buffered everything, and Esplora has no timeout. Needs a user-picked hostile or compromised server; result is memory blowup, freeze or crash of the user's own tab in test-only views, where such a server can already stall or lie. Defense in depth: Low. Same class is documented for BlindBit and relayerClient, not for these clients.
L4-05.fix: fetchTransport is JSON-RPC-only (global fetch, fixed POST), so it is not directly reusable. Add a small shared readCapped(res, maxBytes) (reader loop, cancel on overflow, early reject on Content-Length) and use it at the three sites (Esplora 16 MiB, Tron 8 MiB, Solana e.g. 8 MiB); add a default timeout to EsploraClient.

G1-01.claim: validateInvoice accepts expiresAt, quote.timestamp and quote.expiresAt up to 2^53-1 s, but the Pay review renders them via formatUnix (new Date(s*1000).toISOString()), which throws RangeError for s > 8.64e12. The app has no React error boundary, so a validly signed link carrying such a time unmounts the whole React root instead of failing closed with 'Invoice rejected' (threat model 4.1 D: hostile
G1-01.why: Reproduced at HEAD on the beta-core Pay review: a signed link with expiresAt or fiat-quote times > 8.64e12 s blanks the whole React root via direct link, paste, scanned-QR open and same-tab hashchange, even with no manifest (unknown chain). Per-victim, one click, no funds or keys at risk; reload recovers (autoClearFragment default on). The opener-hashchange vector adds nothing an opener cannot do
G1-01.fix: Minimal: make formatUnix total (invalid Date -> 'invalid date'); covers Pay.tsx:895/900/1201 and PrintableBill:43. Then cap invoice/quote times in validateInvoice at 253402300799 so SDK/CLI/merchant-ledger Date code is safe too, and add a root error boundary as defense in depth. Receipt issuedAt cap is optional (not attacker-reachable). Update THREAT_MODEL 4.1 D.

G1-02.claim: startEmbedHost takes its postMessage origin allowlist from a merchant profile read from the page URL (?gpm=). verifyMerchantProfile only checks a self-signature against the signer key inside the same profile; that key is never pinned or bound to the opened invoice's signer. Anyone can mint a valid profile naming any origin, so the 'signed merchant profile includes this origin' gate (App.tsx/SDK co
G1-02.why: Code facts reproduced: a fresh-key profile naming any origin is accepted and that origin gets gp:init/gp:done. Unreachable as shipped: default bundle compiles startEmbedHost(window,p,!1); a test forbids the flag on Pages; nginx default sends frame-ancestors 'none'; hosting kit cannot express an allowlist; embedding/profiles are later-preserved (LEAN_RELEASE_SCOPE). Needs an operator-reviewed frame
G1-02.fix: Pinning alone is incomplete: a pinned merchant could still frame another seller's invoice, as completion is not bound to it. Better: send gp:done only if the paid invoice's signer equals profile.signer (pass ctx.review.invoice.signer at Pay.tsx:710), show signerFingerprint/'unverified identity' (spec 14), fix the comments. While later-preserved, documenting frame-ancestors as sole gate suffices.

G1-03.claim: parseInvoiceLink documents rejecting IP-literal hosts (loopback only with allowLocalDev) but only tests /^[0-9.]+$/ on the regex-captured host. Hex and mixed IPv4 forms that WHATWG URL parsing maps to IPs pass, including loopback, RFC 1918 and link-local addresses, without allowLocalDev.
G1-03.why: Reproduced: 0x7f000001, 0X7F000001, 0x7f.1, 0x7f.0.0.1, 1.2.3.0x4, 0xa9.0xfe.0xa9.0xfe accepted; decimal/octal/dotted forms rejected. No shipped consumer: package is private, its DEVIATIONS 1 says not integrated, web imports only builders, the web paste path keeps only the fragment, and the web QR wrapper compares to the canonical deployment hostname. allowedHosts ('strongly recommended') already
G1-03.fix: The new URL() comparison is correct. Simpler, dependency-free equivalent: apply WHATWG's 'ends in a number' rule and reject when the host's last label matches /^(?:[0-9]+|0x[0-9a-f]*)$/i (exactly when URL parses it as IPv4), keeping the dev exception for literal 127.0.0.1. Add hex/mixed vectors to negative.test.ts.

G2-01.claim: Documented fix for PRIVACY-E2E-03 does not hold. Audit 17 says BtcView 'initializes outputs unchecked and requires explicit per-output selection', but runScan pre-checks every found output. Review/sign then spends all silent-payment outputs in one transaction, and reviewSweep warns only about fee rate, fee share and own address, never about linkage. Unrelated payments get clustered by common-input
G2-01.why: Reachable by default (nav 'Bitcoin (test)', no flag). runScan pre-checks every output and reviewSweep has no linkage warning, so clicking through with the defaults consolidates payments. Audit 17 marks PRIVACY-E2E-03 closed, but every BtcView.tsx revision in all refs keeps the preselect line, so the closure is false. Live harm is test-coin linkage in a later-preserved view. Medium stands: a docume
G2-01.fix: Right direction, incomplete. Also validate a scanned or pasted destination without needing a selection (BtcView.tsx:371 calls reviewSweep with selected=[] -> INVALID_INPUT). Warn at selection time and in review when >1 input is selected, and say that separate sweeps to one destination also link. Update the 4 tests. Revert audit 17's PRIVACY-E2E-03 row to open.

G2-02.location: apps/web/src/App.tsx:110-128 (no lock hook in features/tron/TronView.tsx, features/solana/SolanaView.tsx, features/btc/BtcView.tsx)
G2-02.claim: The idle lock (lockTimeoutMin, default 15) only locks the tag vault and clears the EVM session. The BTC, Solana and TRON views stay mounted and have no idle or visibility lock of their own. After the timeout their spend and view scalars stay in memory and are not zeroized, the plaintext seed or backup notice stays rendered, and the view can still sign. The only signal is an sr-only 'Seller keys an
G2-02.why: Reachable: chain views are in the default nav and stay mounted while shown. The idle timer only locks tags and clears the EVM session. Settings promises only 'Lock local tags after idle minutes', so no false claim is made. Leaving the view already wipes TRON/Solana keys (not BTC, see G2-04). Needs a user who leaves a chain view open on an unattended unlocked machine. The keys guard test coins in l
G2-02.fix: Add a lockEpoch to AppContext, bumped by the idle timer. Btc/Solana/TronView run their lock() when it changes (BTC needs the G2-04 wipe), and the announcement names them. Do not remount every view (Pay mid-payment). Add the hidden-page timeout (KL-27) once in App, covering the EVM session too. Say in the view that the idle lock forgets unexported test wallets.

G2-03.claim: Chain-view spending secrets (TRON 64-byte spend+view backup, Solana and BTC 32-byte seeds) are rendered in the DOM as soon as a wallet is created, with no reveal step (wallet.ts says 'on request'). They never auto-hide and do not hide when the page is hidden. A one-click Copy writes them to the system clipboard with no warning and no clearing, even after 'Lock and forget keys'. The app's own SECRE
G2-03.why: Reachable by default: 'Create new test wallet' shows the plaintext seed/backup at once. It stays until Hide, Lock or leaving, and Copy puts it on the clipboard with no warning or clear. The qr-colors SECRET rule covers secret QR frames, not this text, so it shows intent rather than a broken control. Beta-core never shows or copies raw keys; these three CopyButtons are the only ones that copy walle
G2-03.fix: Hide by default behind 'Show backup', which can re-reveal while the wallet is loaded (backupHex is recomputable). Auto-hide on visibilitychange or after 60 s. Keep Copy only behind a warning. Run the best-effort writeText('') inside the Lock/Hide click handlers: timer-driven clears lack focus or user activation (Safari, Firefox) and never purge OS clipboard history.

G2-04.claim: BtcView never zeroizes b_scan or b_spend. lock() only drops React state and the unmount effect only aborts. There is no walletRef or wipe as in TronView and SolanaView, and the per-output spendTweak buffers in scan results are never wiped (Solana wipes its tweaks). The header comment says keys 'vanish when you leave the view', but the secret scalars stay intact in the heap until garbage collection
G2-04.why: BtcView has no walletRef or zeroize: Lock and unmount only drop references, and resetFlow drops spendTweak scalars without wiping them, unlike TronView/SolanaView. Exploiting it needs a later heap disclosure (dump, swap, debugger) on a test-only, later-preserved view. The wipe is best-effort anyway: seed hex strings and bigints live until GC (secret.ts:94-100, KL-23/25). Matches the WEB-APP-07 hea
G2-04.fix: Correct and minimal. Add wipeWallet (keys.scanSecret, keys.spendSecret) and wipeFound (spendTweak). Keep walletRef/scanRef and call both in lock(), in resetFlow() before a new scan, and on unmount. Add the TRON/Solana op guard so a late scan result after Lock is wiped, not stored. Test that the buffers are zero. Keep the 'best effort' wording (KL-23).

G2-05.location: apps/web/src/views/SellerKeys.tsx:282 (and every controlled secret input: TronView.tsx:264, SolanaView.tsx:257, BtcView.tsx:214, passphrase fields)
G2-05.claim: Key and passphrase inputs are React-controlled (value={state}), and react-dom 19 mirrors a controlled value into the DOM value attribute. Typed spending keys, seeds, TRON backups and passphrases therefore sit in the markup as value="...", where DevTools Elements, outerHTML or DOM serializers can read them and CSS attribute selectors can match them. SellerKeys clears the raw-key fields only after a
G2-05.why: True (react-dom 19.3.1 mirrors controlled values into the value attribute), but it adds little. The CSP (style-src 'self', img-src 'self' data:) blocks page CSS injection and exfiltration, and anyone with DevTools or an extension can read input.value anyway. The real residue is a key left after a failed import and not cleared by the idle lock, which is open S3-26 ('failed imports leave them') and
G2-05.fix: Minimal: clear secret-field state on failed import and on lock/idle (KL-26). The attribute mirrors state, so this removes it too. Uncontrolled ref inputs (track only emptiness for disabled buttons) are optional hardening. Drop the 'remove the value attribute after each change' alternative: React re-sets defaultValue on every render.

G2-06.claim: The vault save form uses autocomplete=new-password, so browsers offer to generate and save the passphrase. The vault unlock field and the per-sweep step-up field use autocomplete=current-password. Together they invite the browser to store the vault passphrase in the same profile as the IndexedDB vault ciphertext and to autofill the 'required for each sweep action' gate. Meanwhile the UI says that
G2-06.why: Holds in default build (no flag). Real risk: user accepts the browser's save/generate offer for the vault passphrase; after the 15-min idle lock or a reload, one autofill+click restores the spend key to anyone at the profile, which THREAT_MODEL says that party never gets and the UI calls offline-guess only. Tokens aren't the root cause: Chrome/Firefox offer to save password fields even with autoco
G2-06.fix: Only partly effective: browser password managers largely ignore autocomplete=off on password fields. Keep it for KL-14, but rely on: dropping new-password on vault save (no generated password), copy saying 'do not let the browser save this; it defeats the vault and idle lock', and fixing 'never saved'. Consider requiring the vault passphrase for keystore export.

G3-01.claim: Service and webhook HMAC secrets may be stored as ordinary gateway settings (type 'password' in woocommerce_ghostpay_settings); the wp-config constant only wins if defined. WooCommerce returns every gateway setting value verbatim from REST GET /wc/v3/payment_gateways and echoes it into the settings HTML, so any manage_woocommerce principal, including a READ-only REST API key, can read the webhook
G3-01.why: Confirmed against WooCommerce trunk: v2/v3 gateway REST returns raw settings values; GET needs only key permission 'read' plus an owner with manage_woocommerce. A read-only key, or any read-only SQLi/backup of wp_options, yields webhook_secret and lets anyone complete pending orders. Needs secrets typed into the form (README only prefers wp-config). Latent: manual-install plugin, not in the releas
G3-01.fix: Correct. Minimal: read secrets only from GHOSTPAY_*_SECRET constants/getenv and drop both form fields; on upgrade unset stored service_secret/webhook_secret and tell merchants to rotate. If a UI field must stay, keep it in a separate never-echoed option and blank it in woocommerce_rest_prepare_payment_gateway (covers v2+v3). PS: env, not Configuration.

G3-02.claim: amountMinor has no defined exponent. WooCommerce scales the total by wc_get_price_decimals() (a display setting), PrestaShop by Currency::precision (validation.php:36), the reference service example by a fixed 2 (checkout.mjs:38-41,69), but the GhostPay app reads fiat.minorUnits with fiatDecimals(): 0 for 8 listed codes, else 2 (apps/web/src/lib/format.ts:26-30). Any mismatch prices the invoice 10
G3-02.why: Mismatch confirmed with real to_minor, formatFiat and fiatToTokenAmount: plugin scales by WC display decimals (PS: CLDR precision); the app assumes 0 for 8 codes, else 2. Acceptance follows if the service maps amountMinor to fiat.minorUnits (README/example imply) and the event echoes it. Latent: no manifest ships, mainnets disabled, Base Sepolia has no feed so fiat_quote fails closed, plugins out
G3-02.fix: Scale by one ISO-4217 exponent table (not wc_get_price_decimals/Currency::precision) at invoice creation and webhook comparison; to_minor then fails closed only on precision loss (USD at 0 store decimals still gives 4900, so refusing differing store decimals is unneeded). Send the exponent so the service asserts it; complete the app table (FIATD-5).

G3-03.claim: The webhook selects `event_ids` from ghostpay_invoice, but ecc29c1 dropped that column from createInvoiceTable() (ghostpay.php:55-57; present in e4f6825). Every valid webhook fails at the lookup, so the claim/idempotency and amount policy that audit 15 and the README describe are unreachable and no order can ever be marked paid. On PHP 7 (PDO silent) getRow() returns false and the code acks 200 'u
G3-03.why: Ran the real webhook controller over HTTP with a PS 8.2-faithful Db shim and the module's own DDL: every valid event fails at the SELECT. PHP 8: PrestaShopException, 500 on every retry. PHP 7.4 (arrow fns need 7.4; PS ships polyfill-php81): 200 {ok:true}, event dropped. Claim table never used, so audit 15's PS claim fix is unreachable. Fails closed, no forged acceptance; skeleton, not packaged, no
G3-03.fix: Correct: select only `id_order`. Add CI that runs the install DDL and every controller query (SQLite/MySQL) plus both PHP suites (CI runs neither). order_action: pay only from awaiting, PS_OS_ERROR or PS_OS_CANCELED (late payment, as WooCommerce allows); other states get a note. Ignoring every non-awaiting, non-error state would drop late payments.

G3-04.claim: claim_identity() treats add_option() as insert-if-absent, but WordPress add_option() does a non-locking get_option() check, then INSERT ... ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE. Two concurrent deliveries of one event (fresh nonces) both pass the check; the second upsert overwrites the first token and also returns true, so both run apply_event(). The README/audit 15 claim of idempotency across concurrent delive
G3-04.why: Confirmed with the real claim_identity under true multi-process concurrency and WP trunk add_option semantics (check, then INSERT..ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE; 2 rows = true): both deliveries ran payment_complete in 3 of 4 runs; B can overwrite A's completed claim, so both may answer 200. Needs duplicate dispatch inside the check-to-insert window (wider with a persistent object cache). Duplicate side
G3-04.fix: Correct. Claim via $wpdb->query(prepare("INSERT IGNORE INTO {$wpdb->options} (option_name,option_value,autoload) VALUES (%s,%s,'no')")) === 1; read state back with $wpdb->get_var, not get_option (stale notoptions/cache can fool it), then wp_cache_delete. Or a UNIQUE-key claim table created on activation, as in PS. Nonce claim needs no change.

G3-05.claim: Order transitions ignore the order's state and which invoice an event refers to. A sufficient invoice.paid/over on an already-paid order falls into the else branch and sets it on-hold with the note 'payment below the order total'. invoice.expired for a superseded invoice cancels a pending order whose newer invoice (several are allowed per order, :224-225) is still payable.
G3-05.why: Reproduced with the real apply_event: a sufficient invoice.paid on a processing order, and invoice.paid then invoice.over on one invoice, flip the order to on-hold with a false 'below the order total' note; invoice.expired for an older invoice cancels a pending order whose newer invoice (retries are by design, :224) is still payable. Operational only: a later payment still completes the cancelled
G3-05.fix: Correct and minimal: if is_paid(), only add a note (flag double/over payment for refund); use on-hold only when cmp<0 or null on an unpaid order. Cancel on expiry only if the event invoiceId equals the order's last _ghostpay_invoice_id (or a single _ghostpay_current_invoice meta set in process_payment).

G3-06.claim: The example answers a duplicate with 200 while the first delivery of the same event is still inside onEvent(). If that first attempt then fails, it releases the id and returns 500, but the sender already holds a 2xx for the event and stops retrying, so the payment event is lost. The PHP integrations answer a live claim with 503 for exactly this case.
G3-06.why: Confirmed with the real receiver.mjs: a retry arriving while the first delivery is still in onEvent gets 200 duplicate; the first then fails and releases, but the sender already has a 2xx, so the event is never applied. Needs a handler slower than sender timeout plus the 15-30 s first retry (e.g. a 50 s InnoDB lock wait) or parallel duplicate dispatch. Example only, not packaged or in CI; lost ord
G3-06.fix: Correct. Better in merchant-hooks: make IdempotencyGuard tri-state (processing/done) so an in-flight duplicate gets a retryable 409/503, 200 duplicate only after onEvent resolves, release on failure; the receiver just maps states. Keep the note that a durable shared store is needed beyond one process.
